offence_severity: Minimum: 10 years, Maximum: Life imprisonment (Section 302/34 IPC)
physical_harm: The deceased sustained one cut injury on his neck and one minor injury to his finger
number_of_offences: Two offences/counts charged; both were finally upheld by the High Court before being set aside by the Supreme Court
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the prosecution witnesses were tutored by the police, which led to the discarding of their evidence.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as interested and tutored, leading to serious doubt about the genuineness of the prosecution case.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 4th October 2007; Trial judgment: 15.09.2009; High Court decision: 15.09.2009; Supreme Court decision: 05 April 2024
legal_representation: G. Sivabala Murugan, Mailysamy, Selvaraj Mahendran, C.Adhikesavan, P.V. Hari Krishnan, P. Soma Sundaram, R Nedumaran, B Ragunath, Mrs. N.C Kavitha, Vijay Kumar, Advs. for the Appellant; Dr. Joseph Aristotle S., Ms. Shubhi Bhardwaj, Ms. Vaidehi Rastogi, Advs. for the Respondent
procedural_irregularity: Police tutored material prosecution witnesses, which is a gross misuse of power by the police machinery
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted; High Court: Confirmed conviction and life sentence; Supreme Court: Appeals allowed, impugned judgments and orders set aside, appellants acquitted
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the evidence of PW-2 to PW-5 is free of material contradictions and omissions, and that the accused had a clear intention to assault the deceased, leading to the death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution witnesses were tutored by the police, their testimony should be discarded, and that the accused were not present at the incident. They also highlighted the absence of independent eyewitnesses and the prolonged incarceration of the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that tutoring of material witnesses by the police amounts to a gross misuse of power and undermines the judicial process, leading to the rejection of the prosecution's case.
precedent_relied_upon: Gursewak Singh v. Union of India & Anr. [2023] 10 SCR 1139; Ram Manohar Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh [2023] SCC OnLine SC 1084; Ghapoo Yadav & Ors. v. the State of M.P. [2003] 2 SCR 69; Sukhbir Singh v. State of Haryana [2002] 1 SCR 1152; Sandhya Jadhav v. State of Maharashtra [2006] 3 SCR 632; Prakash Chand v. State of H.P. [2004] Supp. 3 SCR 389; Pulicherla Nagaraju v. State of A.P. [2006] Supp. 4 SCR 633
judicial_mitigating_factors: The accused had undergone incarceration for more than 10 years before being enlarged on bail, and the benefit of substantial doubt was given to the appellants.
other_sentence_order: The Director General of Police of Tamil Nadu was directed to conduct an enquiry into the conduct of the police officials who tutored the witnesses, and appropriate action was to be initiated against the erring officials.
